questions.question: In the following question, four number pairs are given. The number on left side of (–) is related to the number on the right side of (–) with some Logic/Rule/Relation. Three are similar on basis of same Logic/Rule/Relation. Select the odd one out from the
questions.solution:
The logic/rule/relation followed here is:

1) 11 - 16 → 11 **+ 5** = 16

2) 13 - 18 → 13 **+ 5** = 18

3) 36 - 41 → 36 **+ 5** = 41

4) 23 - 26 → 23 **+ 3** = 26

Clearly, 23 – 26 doesn’t follows the rule/logic/relation and hence is the odd one out.

questions.question: In the following question, select the odd letter/letters from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
1) TOJE → T **– 5** = O → O **– 5** = J → J **– 5** = E

2) VQLG → V **– 5** = Q → Q **– 5** = L → L **– 5** = G

3) XSNI → X **– 5** = S → S **– 5** = N → N **– 5** = I

4) PKFB → P **– 5** = K → K **– 5** = F → F **– 4** = B

Clearly, PKFB doesn’t follows the pattern and is the odd one out.

questions.question: Mayank remembers that the examination is after 18th December but before 21st December, while Suraj remembers that the examination is before 24th December but after 19th December. On which date of December is the examination?
questions.solution:
Mayank remembers that the examination is after 18th December but before 21st December. So, According to Mayank exam date is 19, **20**

Suraj remembers that the examination is before 24th December but after 19th December. So, According to Suraj exam date is 20, 21, 22, 23

According to both, only 20 December date is common. So, the Exam is on 20 December.

Hence, the examination is on ‘20th December’.

questions.question:
From the given alternatives, select the word which CANNOT be formed using the letters of the given word.

**Tribulations**
questions.solution:
1) Bastion → Tri**b**ul**ations** → Can be formed.

2) Trust → **Tr**ib**ul**a**t**ion**s** → Can be formed.

3) Ribbon → Tribulations → Cannot be formed as one more ‘b’ is required.

4) Slit → Tribu**l**a**ti**on**s **→ Can be formed.

Hence, answer is ‘Ribbon’.

questions.question:
In the question two statements are given, followed by two conclusions, I and II. You have to consider the statements to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions, if any, follows from the given statements.

**Statement I:** No shoes are boots.

**Statement II:** No sneakers are shoes.

**Conclusion I:** Some boots are sneakers.

**Conclusion II:** All sneakers are boots.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor conclusion II follows

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1fd57c75de09adf26d4b4d6ef4779b5d5f131c9c0fc548e0406b260a9552470a.png] 

Conclusion I: Some boots are sneakers → False.

Conclusion II: All sneakers are boots → False.

Hence, Neither Conclusion I nor II follows.
